round: S4-R2 — warm re-entry reliability, listener lifecycle, route recovery
mode: bounded implementation round; every figure below is read from a real browser run

instruments.world: assets/tests/_s3r11-interaction-runner.js — the same fixture world S3-R11 and S4-R1 used

what_is_authoritative: REQUEST COUNTS and the actions behind them — a property of control flow, true at any server speed.
RENDERED ROW COUNTS — the harness serves a narrower world for one generation, so the number on screen names which response committed.
FRESHNESS STATE — read from window.srdFreshness(), which the page sets and nothing else writes.
LIVE LISTENER COUNTS BY TARGET — window, document, and elements still connected to the document at measurement time.
ORDERING — what was on screen at the moment the section became visible, and how much had settled by then.

what_is_not_observable.milliseconds: NOT_OBSERVABLE. S4-R1 measured why: under --virtual-time-budget Chrome freezes both performance.now() and Date.now() while a task runs, and process-level deltas sit inside an 840 ms baseline spread. §11 asks for ordering where this is so, and ordering is what is recorded.

instrument_caveats: S4-R1 counted addEventListener minus removeEventListener across the whole process. That is a CALL LEDGER, not a leak: a handler bound to a table row that innerHTML then discards is unreachable and costs nothing. This round classifies every registration by target and counts only those still reachable — window, document, or an element still in the document. The two instruments disagree for that reason, and the by-target one is the honest number.

The first version of the re-entry wait exited as soon as any terminal-looking surface appeared, including the empty box painted during a failure. Readings taken after it were mid-flight and looked like permanent loading. The wait now requires no outstanding request for the page plus the same terminal state observed three times, and every figure here comes from that version.
WeakRef holds the listener targets, so the instrument cannot itself be the reason an element survives to be counted.

baseline.note: The same instrument against the tree before this round, for the three claims that are repairs rather than confirmations.
baseline.refreshFailureDestroysModel: YES — _srdRenderError_ began by nulling the read-model, so a refresh that failed over good rows discarded them. There was no scenario in which rows survived a failed refresh, because there was no branch that could keep them.
